key_insight: PoreML unifies pore-scale data generation, model training, and evaluation to make multiphase flow prediction in porous media more reliable and reproducible.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports applications such as CO2 storage, fuel cells, and packaging by enabling data-driven models that can predict interface evolution in complex porous structures.
method: GPU-native lattice Boltzmann solver for reproducible pore-scale simulation data
3.3 TB dataset with 560 runs and 158,546 time steps across four scenarios
Unified benchmarking for one-step prediction, rollout stability, and physical consistency
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a large open dataset spanning synthetic and micro-CT-derived geometries, plus domain-specific evaluation protocols and transfer tests to larger domains and real-material structures.
watch_item: Performance may still depend strongly on dataset coverage, wettability settings, and geometry transfer beyond the scenarios included in PoreML.
paper_title: PoreML: A Data-Driven Framework for Learning Multiphase Flow in Porous Media
